text: US stocks fell sharply Thursday as the AI-led selloff deepened and Nvidia's strong results failed to restore sentiment. The S&P 500 dropped 2.0% to 7,175.83, its sixth straight loss, while the Nasdaq fell 2.3% to 23,879.20 and the Dow lost 2.2% to 49,097.06, closing below 50,000. Weak jobless claims and Philadelphia Fed data, rate-hike pricing, a 7.7% drop in AMD and a rough debut for the Anthropic IPO weighed on sentiment, and the S&P 500 ETF is down about 5% on the week. The TSX closed at 34,028.73, down 1.6%. In Europe the STOXX 600 was down about 0.2% in midsession trade, and Asian moves were mixed; official closes for Europe and Asia on this date were not found.
mood: Risk-off: AI valuation worries, rate-hike expectations and weak US data drove a broad global selloff despite Nvidia's earnings beat.

veqt.t: Broad selloff: S&P 500 -2.0% (sixth straight loss), Nasdaq -2.3%, Dow -2.2% and below 50,000.
TSX fell 1.6% to 34,028.73, following Wall Street lower.
STOXX 600 was down about 0.2% in midsession trade; closing figures for Europe, Japan and Australia were not found.
